post.0:
I won 83 to Dee's 72 by owning magenta all game and then stripping the table bare at the start of round III. The decider was my opening double turn in III: Lie Low first so nobody could steal or poach from me for the round, then Greatest Hits firing Con Men and Accomplice for an 8-steal that took literally every resource my rivals held. That handed me the lead in all four colors, and I spent my next placement on Build Up because green had no other space to answer with, which locked a second +10. Round II's two Shake Downs on a broke Ben (Martyrs, then Line Cutters via Reprise) were the quieter swing that put me in range. My mistake was round I: I opened Help Yourself into an open Echo and Dee simply copied my steal back off me.

META: The contest race plus theft makes every round a real fight over who holds what at the bell, and Lie Low, Shake Down and Farewell create sharp, readable decisions. What isn't working is that the copy spaces (Echo, Encore, Greatest Hits, Reprise) make On Recruit steals like Con Men and Accomplice repeat over and over, so a player with no resources and no members ends up with nothing to do and nothing to lose, as Ben did. Buying followers only in 1/5/10 packs also strands leftovers on everyone's last turn. The first thing I'd change is to stop copy effects from replaying a rival's On Recruit steals (or cap Encore and Greatest Hits to non-steal effects).
post.1:
I lost badly, last with 35, and it was decided in round II when Ava's Shake Down and then her Reprise copy of Shake Down took Martyrs and Line Cutters off me in one round, because I was broke and couldn't pay either cost. From then on I had no members and no engine, and every pile I built got stolen the next turn: Help Yourself in round I, Con Men copied by Encore, Echo and Greatest Hits in round III. The best decision I made was cashing 11 resources into 10 followers early in round III, since Cal and Dee both went raiding right after. I tried to swing late as the last placer in round II and on blue in round III, but both times a rival placed after me and could tie or answer. Ava won by holding Lie Low in round III (immune to theft) while Greatest Hits fired Con Men and Accomplice for an 8-steal; nobody could touch her pile.

META: The contest economy and the color-by-color holding tension are working, and conversion spaces like Exchange make last turns interesting. What isn't working is that theft is so dense (Help Yourself, Crime Wave, Shake Down, Poach, plus every copy space repeating Con Men and Accomplice) that a player who falls behind round one gets stripped every turn and has no way back; being broke also makes Shake Down a free member. The one thing I'd change first: stop On Recruit steals (Con Men, Accomplice) being copyable by Encore, Echo and Greatest Hits, or make Reprise unable to repeat Shake Down and Poach.

I finished third with 63, and my engine was quietly fine for two rounds but never turned into contest wins. The real loss was round II: I spent down to 3 blue on my last Recruit Twice and Ava's Peek took the +6 blue off me, then in round III Dee's Poach plus Reprise-on-Poach took Snobs and Patroness in one double turn, Estate Sale turned my Patroness into 8 white for her, and from then on every Trendsetters bury I did paid Dee a follower. Ava won by holding magenta and green under Lie Low where nobody could steal, then cashing Martyrs through Farewell and buying 10s. The between-rounds sweep and Scouts never triggered Bargain Bin or Patroness, which undercut the plan I'd picked my artifact for. Buying followers with Regular (pay 1, get the blue back) was my best late-game line, which says something about how flat members are compared to straight follower buys in round III.
